On Thu, Jan 31, 2013 at 2:28 PM, <pesc...@fastmail.fm> wrote:
Hi,

I am certainly doing something basically wrong, but I can't figure it out.  I have a large dataset that I am subsetting to make graphs.  The dataset is in long form.  
I can make the graphs below, individually, but when I try to put them on a single page with grid.arrange, I get:
Error: No layers in plot

I get the same error using the multiplot function. 

I can also save either of these plots separately.  

(Note: I am not the sharpest code writer and I have a fairly thick skin.  Any suggestions are welcome) 

Thanks.

library("ggplot2") 
library("scales") 
library("gridExtra") 



CAspec <- read.csv(file="CA_BCG4.csv", h=T) 
RHCA_p_oca <- CAspec[CAspec$FishID == "RHCA" & CAspec$NEWBASIN == "Ohio", ] 
RHCA_p_all <- CAspec[CAspec$FishID == "RHCA" , ] 

p1<- ggplot(RHCA_p_oca,aes(ProbRefState,fish_prop)) 
p1+geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2))+ 
  stat_smooth(method="loess")+ 
  scale_color_brewer(palette="Paired")+scale_size(range=c(2,10))+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1))+ 
  labs(title="CA_RHCA Proportions", x="State Prob. Ref.", y="Proportion", colour="Temperature", size="Watershed Area (MI2)") 

p2<- ggplot(RHCA_p_all,aes(ProbRefState,fish_prop)) 
p2+geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2))+ 
  stat_smooth(method="loess")+ 
  scale_color_brewer(palette="Paired")+scale_size(range=c(2,10))+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1))+ 
  labs(title="All_RHCA Proportions", x="State Prob. Ref.", y="Proportion", colour="Temperature", size="Watershed Area (MI2)") 

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol=1) 

--

messages.subject: Re: multiple plots on a page from sub-setted data
parts:
Louis, 

Generally it's better to reply to the list so others have an opportunity to help as well. That being said, I know why you get the error. 
#In the first line you are defining "rhca1". 
rhca1 <- ggplot(RHCA_p_oca,aes(Value,fish_prop))

#but, here... you add the "layers" to the plots. 
rhca1+geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2))+ yadayadayada

For each one of these, simply add... 

rhca1<- rhca1+geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2))
Then it works just fine. 
B

grid.arrange(rhca1, rhca2, ncol=1)

messages.author: 3cb22ac1f2fb38cc
messages.subject: Re: multiple plots on a page from sub-setted data
parts:
Thanks, Brian, Baptiste and Brandon.

After some futzing around, I got the following to work using the arrange and then a tip from one of Baptiste's old posts on saving to a file from a grob (saving to pdf worked - jpg did not).

I did not write my original code correctly as I did not understand layers as well as I thought.

ETVA_p_oca <- CAspec[CAspec$FishID == "ETVA" & CAspec$NEWBASIN == "Ohio", ]
ETVA_p_all <- CAspec[CAspec$FishID == "ETVA" , ]
 
ETVA_pl_ca <-
  ggplot(ETVA_p_oca,aes(ProbRefState,fish_prop))+
  geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2), alpha=1/2)+stat_smooth(method="loess")+
  scale_color_manual(values=pal3)+scale_size(range=c(2,10))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1))+scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  labs(title="CA_ETVA Proportions", x="Probability of Site Being Reference", y="Proportion", colour="Temperature", size="Watershed Area (MI2)")
 
ETVA_pl_all <-
  ggplot(ETVA_p_all,aes(ProbRefState,fish_prop))+
  geom_jitter(aes (colour=D_TEMPCL3, size=MI2), alpha=1/2)+stat_smooth(method="loess")+
  scale_color_manual(values=pal3)+scale_size(range=c(2,10))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1))+scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  labs(title="All_ETVA Proportions", x="Probability of Site Being Reference", y="Proportion", colour="Temperature", size="Watershed Area (MI2)")
  
p <- arrangeGrob(ETVA_pl_ca, ETVA_pl_all)
grid.draw(p)
ggsave("ETVA.pdf", p)
